_what: Notes on how the certified engine builds the PolicyEngine counterpart, shared by every certified-pair result in lane uk-childcare-100k (CenTax and CBP claims alike). Each cites the engine file it was read from at the pin (policyengine-uk 2.89.2). The measured numbers that go with them are written onto each result by scorecard_db/ingest_uk_childcare_100k.py from the artifact beside this file, not copied here.

annotations.text: policyengine-uk 2.89.2 switches a child's universal and targeted hours off once the family is eligible for the extended hours, and values the extended hours at the family's drawn weekly usage (maximum_extended_childcare_hours_usage). The counterpart sums all three entitlements, so the universal hours a newly eligible family loses are netted out rather than double-counted. policyengine-uk#1930 changed this after the pin (closed 12 October 2026).

The offer starts at 9 months. The engine's extended-hours scale starts at age 0.75, but no child under 1 receives extended hours on this pair in any year. microcosm#1126 records that ages are whole years, so 9-11-month-olds never qualify.
annotations.basis: policyengine_uk 2.89.2 parameters/gov/dfe/extended_childcare_entitlement/hours.yaml (threshold 0.75 from 2025); results/uk/childcare_100k/<variant>.json counts.children_under_one_receiving_extended (0 in every world and year); https://github.com/PolicyEngine/microcosm/issues/1126
